swiftMeta: Websites and online stores for cafés, shops, clubs and service businesses. Led by Eli Mitchell with a small team. Currently in Vietnam, working with clients abroad.
stackMeta: Business apps, databases, staff systems and client portals, with AI where it saves work. Led by Eli Mitchell with a small team. You deal with Eli directly.
swiftIntro: For cafés, shops, clubs and service businesses that need customers to find them, see what they offer and get in touch.
heroDetail: Work directly with me. I lead the design, the technical decisions and the delivery, with a small team behind me.
stackIntro: I design and build databases, staff systems and client portals that bring your information together, with AI added where it saves work.
showcaseIntro: Websites designed and built by SwiftSites. Different businesses, distinct identities.
capheSummary: The character of a café, brought online: photography, the menu and coworking information for an international audience.
retroSummary: A bold look, with guides to the incense and tie-dye ranges and a simple way to ask about an order.
rugbySummary: A club’s personality, with clear information for players and visitors from around the world.
capheHeading: A Da Nang café, open to the world.
capheBrief: Càphê Commune brings coffee, breakfast and coworking together in Da Nang. Its website needed to carry the atmosphere and make the useful details easy to find.
capheApproach: Real photography gives the website its character. Clear routes to the menu, coworking and visitor information make it useful. Five language versions welcome an international audience.
capheResult: A photographic website with an illustrated coffee menu, coworking information and practical visit details in English, Vietnamese, Russian, Simplified Chinese and Spanish.
validatorHeading: Purchase-order checking: a reported 50% cut in administration time.
validatorSummary: A tool that checks purchase-order data, sorts it into clean, flagged and blocked, and lets the reviewer concentrate on the exceptions.
validatorBrief: Checking purchase-order information by hand takes time. The screen has to show at a glance what is ready, what is flagged and what needs a person.
validatorApproach: The tool checks each item against the rules and sorts it into three piles: clean, flagged, blocked. A person reviews the flagged ones; the tool never decides alone.
validatorResult: Eli reports that this workflow now takes half the time it did. Purchase-order administration time had been tracked for several staff in the role over a number of years; after the tool went in, the same work took half as long. That figure is for this one workflow; another workflow would need its own measurement.
reported: Reported by Eli for this workflow; not independently audited.
sampleData: Interface concept with sample data. No client records.
swiftServicesIntro: Design and build are planned together, by the same people. Pick the service that fits what your business needs.
stackServicesTitle: Build the system your work actually needs.
stackServicesIntro: Start with the problem. Agree what to build. Build it, test it, hand it over to your team.
webDesc: A website made for your business that explains what you offer and gives visitors a clear way to enquire.
webScope: Usually 5 to 8 pages, works on phones and desktops, one clear path to enquire, an agreed page structure, and the technical basics search engines need.
flagshipDesc: A full redesign of a larger website: page structure, visual direction and launch planned together with you.
flagshipScope: Page structure and content plan, a visual direction made for you, richer interaction, and a plan for moving the existing content and links. Integrations and content production are agreed before the build.
commerceDesc: Online stores built around your products, your customers and the way you work, on an established commerce platform or fully custom.
commerceScope: A bespoke storefront and setup on an agreed commerce platform: catalogue structure, product pages, mobile checkout, payment and delivery configuration, and operator training. Inventory, accounting, booking or fulfilment integrations are scoped where needed. Platform choice follows the requirements; fully custom commerce and complex integrations need discovery and a separate scope. Platform subscriptions, transaction fees and third-party costs are separate.
seoDesc: Find the technical and content changes that could help people discover your website through search and AI answers.
seoScope: An audit, a prioritised list of actions and a walkthrough of the findings. Doing the work is quoted separately. The audit covers where you could appear in AI answers too (GEO and AEO); no ranking or AI citation is guaranteed.
careDesc: Monitoring, maintenance and an agreed allowance for smaller website changes.
careScope: Monitoring, maintenance and a specified allowance for smaller changes. Support windows, hosting and third-party costs are agreed in the proposal.
appDesc: An app on a proper database for one workflow: who uses it, what they can see and do, and how it is handed over are agreed up front.
appScope: One main workflow with its data, users and permissions: a database app, a staff workspace or a client portal. Moving existing data, reports, connections to other systems, testing and handover to the people who run it are agreed in the scope. Large migrations and several systems at once are quoted separately.
platformDesc: Several workflows, user roles and your existing systems joined up, built in agreed stages.
platformScope: Several workflows, roles or connections, delivered in agreed milestones. Which data moves, what depends on what and who needs access are worked out in discovery.
aiDesc: Pick one task AI could do for you, build it, and test it on real examples before using it more widely.
aiScope: Assess where AI would help, build one bounded use, test it on real examples, and add human checking and a fallback for when it gets things wrong. Model costs and ongoing support are quoted separately.
consultDesc: Help deciding what to build, what to buy and what to change: a look at your current systems and clear recommendations.
consultScope: One defined question, agreed preparation and clear recommendations: build or buy, how your systems are doing, where AI would help, and a practical plan. Doing the work is a separate scope.
trainingDesc: Workshops and hands-on exercises for the people who will use or run the system.
trainingScope: Workshops, hands-on exercises and written guidance for an agreed group. Consultancy helps you decide; training helps your team do the work. Neither includes building anything.
opsDesc: Monitoring, maintenance and handling of problems, with agreed support hours and response times.
opsScope: Monitoring, maintenance, handling problems when they come up, and checking AI output where relevant. Each plan states support hours, response times, what work is included and usage costs.
discoveryDesc: A look at your current system, then agreed priorities, constraints and an estimate for building in stages.
discoveryScope: Where things stand now, what matters most, what limits you, and a phased scope with a build estimate. The decisions you need before committing to a bigger build.
aiEditorialTitle: Where AI earns its place: handling documents, sorting enquiries, finding answers in your own records, reporting. Where it does not: anywhere nobody checks the output.
aiEditorial: The aim is to use AI where it makes the work better, not to put it everywhere. I can assess your systems, build and support the right changes, or train your team to run them.

founderTitle: You deal with the person responsible for the work.
founderSwift: I'm Eli Mitchell. I lead design and development at SwiftSites, with a small team I chose myself, which grows carefully as we take on more work. I set the design direction, check the technical quality and deliver the work, and you deal with me directly.
founderStack: I'm Eli Mitchell. I build databases, staff systems and client apps that turn scattered information into something people can rely on. The cases on this site show the kind of work: tools built around a real workflow, under real constraints. I lead a small team I chose myself, and I set the design, check the technical quality and deliver the work.
founderGlobal: I have clients on four continents. I'm in Vietnam at the moment, working remotely, and I can travel for larger projects where time on site makes a difference.
onsiteTitle: Some projects are better understood in person.
onsiteIntro: Watching the work happen shows what a written brief leaves out. For the right projects I can come to you: to assess, run workshops or build on site.
onsiteDetails: Tell me where you are, what needs to change and who would be involved. We'll agree whether a visit is worth it before setting scope, dates and travel.
travelNote: Available to travel for suitable larger projects. Travel and engagement terms are agreed separately.
processTitle: Clear decisions. Progress you can see.

step2Text: Review the page structure and visual direction together before development begins.
step3Text: Build in agreed stages, test the real journeys and review progress together.
step4Text: A clear handover, written-down responsibilities and the right support afterwards.

retroBrief: Back to the 70’s & Beyond is a gift shop and coffee spot on Waiheke Island. The website brings its range and character online while helping visitors find products and ask about an order.
retroApproach: An animated hand-lettered opening, retro illustration and warm colour reflect the shop’s identity. Category price guides and a fragrance guide put practical information alongside the visual character.
retroResult: A website with product and fragrance guides, an order-enquiry builder, visit information and a mobile experience. Selected items become an email enquiry to the shop, rather than a completed online purchase.
rugbyBrief: Da Nang Guerilla Rugby Club needed an online home for its club story and clear information for new players and visiting teams.
rugbyApproach: A cinematic opening and real team photography express the club’s personality. Training information and a WhatsApp joining guide make the first steps clear, with separate enquiry routes for visiting teams, kit and sponsors.
rugbyResult: A seven-language club website with a cinematic opening, team-tour and camp enquiries, kit and sponsor enquiries, and women’s team recruitment information.
